title: Emerging Markets Lead – MENA (Arabic speaking)
description:
ABOUT COLUMN

For companies building financial technology and transforming the financial services space, the biggest bottleneck to their growth and innovation is often the underlying banks and infrastructure stack they rely on. We have spent our careers founding and scaling companies like Plaid, Square, Meta, Blend, and Affirm, and have seen this problem firsthand - builders and developers needing to partner with traditional banks, and creating API and abstraction layers over the patchwork that is the bank, its core, and many other vendors. All of this results in a complex (and often expensive) banking supply chain involving a user, fintech, BaaS middleware provider, bank, core and the Federal Reserve.

At Column, we set out to simplify and fix this. We are a bank and a software company built from the ground up, offering builders and developers technology-forward banking solutions that cut out the hundreds of vendors, middleware providers, and abstraction layers. This means a safer, more transparent, and less costly banking supply chain. Come build with us!

THE OPPORTUNITY

As Column’s Emerging Markets Lead, you will spearhead one of our most strategic international expansion initiatives. In this role, you will be responsible for driving 0-to-1 growth for a new banking product, with a particular focus on building and nurturing relationships with prospective partners and customers in select markets, with a specific focus on markets within MENA. This role combines global expansion strategy, business development with hands-on relationship management, requiring a general business athlete who thrives on networking and executing complex partnerships. This is a unique opportunity to be on the founding team for a new business line, with significant autonomy and direct impact on Column’s global expansion strategy.

This position will be based in Dubai with regular travel throughout the region and occasional travel to Column’s headquarters in San Francisco.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Lead regional market development: Own the end-to-end process of identifying, evaluating, and executing on high-value partnerships with banks across a number of international markets.

- Build and maintain key relationships: Serve as the primary relationship owner for prospective and existing customers, conducting regular in-person meetings, attending local industry events, and managing ongoing partnership development.

- Own partnership execution: Lead complex deal processes from initial outreach through contract signature, working collaboratively with Column’s Legal, Compliance, and Product teams.

- Develop market intelligence: Gather and synthesize insights on local market conditions, regulatory developments, competitive landscape, and customer needs to inform Column’s regional strategy.

- Market expertise and network: Become an expert on the correspondent banking space in our key emerging markets and build an extensive network within their banking and fintech ecosystems.

- Drive operational excellence: Build scalable processes for onboarding, relationship management, and ongoing support that can be replicated as we expand.

 

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

- 6+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, growth, operations or strategy in a high-caliber environment

- 4+ years of business experience specifically in MENA

- Native fluency in Arabic and experience managing business relationships with Arabic-speaking clients and stakeholders

- Track record of successfully managing complex partnerships and high-value deals with executive stakeholders

- Natural networker who thrives on building trust and long-term relationships with senior executives, market experts and decision-makers

- Strong strategic thinking - ability to assess market opportunities, evaluate potential partners, and provide strategic recommendations to senior leadership

Langfuse has grown mostly through product-led, open-source adoption. We built a strong product, wrote useful docs and examples, stayed close to users, shipped in public, and helped developers understand how to build better AI applications.

However, many of the highest-signal moments happen in person: hallway conversations, workshops, meetups, dinners, conference demos, and technical talks.

We want someone who can own that motion end to end; put Langfuse in the right AI engineering rooms, make the product clear to technical audiences, and turn in-person conversations into durable marketing momentum.

We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com http://Booking.com, H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

As Director, Strategic Customer Relations, you will own the strategy, operations, and outcomes of Imprint's customer escalations and back office functions. This is a senior leadership role with direct accountability for building and scaling a best-in-class escalations operation.

You will serve as the vision-setting, execution-driving leader across four core function areas: escalations, back office operations, credit reporting, and social media support - translating reactive, ad hoc processes into a structured, metrics-driven function with a clear roadmap for what great looks like.

- Own strategy, operations, and outcomes across escalations (organic, executive, and partner), back office functions, credit reporting, and social media support

title: AI Service Analyst
description:
AI Service Analyst
ICS.AI · Remote (UK), occasional travel to Basingstoke and client sites
· Full-time, permanent · £26,500 - £30,000 · Entry level / graduate
Build the AI agents that run our service desk - not reset passwords.
ICS.AI is a UK AI consultancy delivering AI transformation to the public sector - local government, higher education and the wider public estate. Our clients commit to transformation on the strength of savings guarantees, and we are held to contractual service levels once our solutions are live. That makes our service data a commercial asset, not admin overhead.
We are hiring an AI Service Analyst to own the day-to-day operation of our service management function, and to build it properly from the ground up. You will be the single point of coordination between clients raising issues, the delivery and engineering teams who resolve them, and the Customer Success team who own the relationship.
This is a first or second role. You do not need to be able to fix the technology. You need to be able to work out what is actually happening, get it to the right person, and tell the client the truth about it clearly and on time.
What you’ll be doing

• Running our Zendesk platform end to end - reviewing every incoming ticket, categorising and prioritising it against a consistent ITIL-aligned model, assigning it to the right resolver and chasing it to closure.

• Early triage on live AI solutions: checking Azure service health, interrogating voice and language platforms, and reproducing what a client is reporting before it consumes a specialist’s time.

• Problem management and root cause analysis - spotting patterns across incidents, assigning causes, and authoring RCA documents that go to clients.

• Client communication and service reporting: proactive updates, SLA tracking, the weekly report pack, and service content for monthly and quarterly reviews.

• Monthly trend analysis across the client portfolio, and the structured feedback loop from live service into our product roadmap.

• Designing, building, shadow-running and tuning AI agents inside Zendesk for triage, classification and first response - including the guardrails that decide what an agent is never allowed to handle alone.

What makes this different from a service desk role
You will not be resetting passwords. Our tickets concern live AI solutions serving citizens and council staff - conversational assistants, voice services, agents and data platforms. And a genuine part of the job is building AI agents to handle the queue: that is what lets the function absorb a growing client base without growing headcount, and it is the difference between this post and a conventional service desk appointment. It is no-code work, but it needs someone who will iterate patiently rather than accept the first output.
What we’re looking for
We are not screening on a degree classification or a specific subject. What we care about is evidence of the following:

• Excellent written English - clear, accurate and appropriate for a professional client audience.

• Strong organisational discipline, and the ability to hold many open items without losing any of them.

• An analytical mindset; comfortable with numbers and spotting patterns.

• Confidence and composure in direct contact with clients by email, phone and video, including when they are unhappy.

• Competence with Microsoft 365, particularly Excel.

• A genuine interest in AI and in how technology is used in public services.

• Eligibility to work in the UK. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Nice to have

• ITIL 4 Foundation - not required at appointment; we will fund it within your first three months.

• Any exposure to a ticketing platform (Zendesk, ServiceNow, Freshdesk, Jira Service Management), including a placement year.

• Experience of local government, higher education or the wider public sector.

• Familiarity with generative AI tools, or any experience of configuring or prompting them

title: Security Engineer - Platform Security
description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

The Platform Security team (PlatSec) defends Plaid against attackers. We own laptop security, cloud security, AI security, detection and response, and red teaming. Right now we're in growth mode. AI has expanded Plaid's attack surface faster than most security teams can adapt, and we're building the guardrails, identity controls, and detection systems to keep pace without slowing the business down. If you like solving problems nobody's solved yet, this is that team.

About the role
You'll be Plaid's first line of defense on AI security. You'll review new AI technologies to find security risks before they ship, then design and implement the controls that close them. You'll build the guardrails, identity management, and detection systems that let Plaid use AI aggressively without getting burned.

Responsibilities

- Review AI systems and integrations for security risk before and after deployment.

- Design and deploy guardrails, sandboxes, and other controls that contain what AI agents can do.

- Build or implement systems to track and manage AI identities, so we know what access every AI has been granted and can balance risk with agility.

- Detect and mitigate prompt injection across Plaid's AI surface area.

- Run AI-focused security reviews and set the bar other teams build to.

- Your impact: fewer AI-related incidents, faster AI shipping, and controls that scale. Plaid wants to be a leader in AI, internally and externally, and we can’t do that safely without you.

Qualifications
Must-have: hands-on experience securing AI technologies, including at least one of:

- deploying guardrails or sandboxes,

- managing AI identities,

- detecting or mitigating prompt injection,

- running AI security reviews, or

- implementing AI security tooling (built or bought).

- Nice-to-haves:

- Experience at a frontier AI lab or on a security team defending production AI systems at scale.

- Experience on a Infrastructure Security, Cloud Security, Platform Security, Corporate Security, Security Operations (SecOps), and/or Detection & Response team

- Software security review, SDLC, vulnerability discovery, and/or offensive security experience

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

TO BE A TEYAN

We are not just a fintech company. We develop people by giving them the autonomy and the responsibility to challenge the status quo, so they can be the main actors of the change we want to bring to the market.

We are always looking for people better than us to join the team, disrupt payments, and revolutionise commerce in Europe. The goal we share, the mission is one, and at the end of the day we are just people trying to help other people.

WHAT IS YOUR MISSION?

Our sales agents are on the front lines, talking to merchants every day. Across the go to market systems they use to manage their sales, HubSpot CRM is where their deals, activities, conversations, reporting, automations and portfolio lives. When HubSpot works, our salespeople sell. When it breaks quietly in the background, deals stall, data drifts, and the people who trust the numbers stop trusting the tool.

Your mission is to be the guardian of that system. You are the person who keeps HubSpot healthy, honest, and trustworthy, so that every seller and every leader can rely on it without ever thinking about it.

This is not a caretaking job where you wait for tickets and tick them off. You are a detective and a builder. You go looking for what is wrong before anyone reports it, you find the real reason something failed instead of patching the symptom, and you make sure the same failure never happens twice. You turn a messy, growing CRM into a system people can trust, and you can prove it with data.

AS THE GUARDIAN OF OUR CRM YOU WILL

Investigate root causes, not symptoms. When something in HubSpot fails, you own it. You dig into what actually went wrong, validate the real root cause, and drive it to a fix. You are the single point of contact when the CRM misbehaves, and nothing gets dropped on your watch.

Prevent the next bug before it happens. You do not just close errors, you learn from them. You spot the patterns, harden the implementations that keep breaking, and put guardrails in place so a whole class of problems disappears. Every automation and implementation, local or global, follows our guidelines because you make sure it does, before and after it goes live.

Measure the health of the CRM. You build the dashboards that show, at a glance, whether what we ship actually works and keeps working. You track error rates, adoption, and data quality over time, so CRM health stops being a feeling and becomes a number we can watch and improve.

Turn data into action. You are as comfortable reading the numbers as fixing the system. You globalise and clean up our reporting once the requirements from Commercial Excellence are aligned, retire the dashboards no one needs, and use data to find the problems no one has noticed yet.

Build and improve, hands on. You create new automations and refine the ones we have, you read the logic of a workflow well enough to debug it, and you keep the instance clean, governed, and scalable across every market in Europe.

At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable.  

We're looking for a motivated and driven IT Infrastructure Engineer (m/f/d) who will help us shape our team, drive the company to the next level, and have a direct influence on our success.

As an IT Infrastructure Engineer, you lead the efforts of maintaining and improving our global identity and access management platform as a coherent set of highly available services following our cloud-focused strategy. It is your responsibility to identify improvement opportunities, drive identity projects, and build a unified, scalable environment.

Based in Germany and the US, our IT Infrastructure Services team designs, implements, and manages global cloud and on-premises infrastructure solutions to provide Flix with internal business services such as identity and access management, security and compliance configuration, communication tools, file sharing, 3rd-level support, and infrastructure consulting.

About the Role

• Integrate new internal and external applications into our identity infrastructure (e.g., SSO ) following best practices

• Work on projects to improve internal role-based access control concepts

• Consult other teams and guide them to success, leveraging our services especially regarding identity and access management

• Drive innovation and improve our services together with the team

• Automate recurring tasks

• Design the future IT infrastructure of Flix

About You

• At least 3 years of experience with Microsoft Entra ID or similar identity and access management platforms

• Advanced knowledge of modern authentication protocols ( OIDC , OAuth 2.0, and SAML )

• At least 3 years of scripting experience (ideally with Python)

• At least 1 year of experience with IaC solutions (preferably Terraform)

• Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools to streamline infrastructure automation, troubleshooting, and daily operations

• Basic experience using APIs

• Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is a plus

• Experience working with IaaS solutions is a plus

• Basic knowledge of modern frontend frameworks (e.g., React) or web technologies is a plus

• Experience with M365 products (such as Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams) is a plus

We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!  

What We Offer

• Travel perks : 12 free Flix vouchers + 12 discount vouchers for friends & family. 

• Work from (M)Anywhere : Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. 

• Hybrid work model : We are an office-first company, but we offer flexibility to balance work and life. 

• Wellbeing support : Access confidential 1:1 counselling, courses, and stress management for yourself and up to four family members. 

• Learning & Development : Take advantage of language classes, training courses, and expert-led sessions to grow your skills. 

• Mentoring Program : Connect with experienced colleagues to gain insights and accelerate your career. 

To view more local benefits specific to each office location, please check out this link:   Locations - Flix Career

Why Join Flix?

At Flix, you’ll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture - giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path.
As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work.

If you’re ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you!

title: Senior Software Engineer - Planner GPU Compute
description:
Zoox made the world’s first purpose-built commercial robotaxi, combining advanced self-driving hardware and software. In order to ensure safe operation, low latency and consistent resource utilization are critical. The Planner Compute team is responsible for the performance of the largest single software component within the autonomy stack, the motion planner. 
The Planner Compute team is looking for an expert in GPU performance. You will instrument, monitor, analyze and optimize GPU-based algorithms that are performance-critical for our solution. The scope for GPU usage ranges from machine learning inference to custom CUDA kernels written specifically for the motion planner.

There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.
 
Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

title: Software Engineer - Postgres
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset - who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

The Snowflake Postgres team is building a managed Postgres experience inside Snowflake. This role is focused on the control plane, where you have the opportunity to work on both on distributed systems at scale and also to work on research grade optimizations at various layers of the software stack including but not limited to provisioning, managing, securing, and operating Postgres in Snowflake. You will work on core backend systems that sit at the intersection of distributed systems, database infrastructure, security, and operational excellence.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Design and build backend services that power provisioning, lifecycle management, and configuration of Snowflake Postgres instances.

- Develop features in the access and user model, including authorization, secure administration flows, and customer-facing management capabilities.

- Improve the reliability, observability, and operability of asynchronous workflows and background systems that keep the service healthy.

- Partner with product, security, and adjacent engineering teams to deliver simple customer experiences on top of complex infrastructure.

- Investigate production issues, participate in on-call, and drive fixes that improve resilience and reduce operational burden.

- Contribute to technical design, code review, and mentoring while helping raise the engineering bar across the team.

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

- 2+ years of experience building production software in backend, infrastructure, or distributed systems environments.

- Strong programming skills in one or more of Java, Go, C++, or Python.

- Strong computer science fundamentals, including concurrency, networking, APIs, and data structures.

- Experience designing and operating reliable services in production, including debugging, monitoring, and incident response.

- Experience working across technical boundaries with product, security, and other engineering teams.

- BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

NICE TO HAVE:

- Experience with PostgreSQL, database internals, or managed database platforms.

- Experience with identity, authorization, RBAC, or other security-sensitive systems.

- Experience with cloud infrastructure on AWS, Azure, or GCP.

- Experience with workflow orchestration, control plane systems, or highly asynchronous service architectures.

WHY JOIN THIS TEAM?

- Work on a strategic product area that expands Snowflake into transactional and operational database workloads

- Build systems that directly shape how customers create, manage, and secure Postgres inside Snowflake

- Tackle a mix of product engineering, infrastructure, reliability, and security problems.

- Join a collaborative team with meaningful ownership, strong technical challenges, and room to grow

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Training - CA
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense

• Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

• Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

• Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing

• Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end

• Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think

• Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code

• Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)

• Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading

• Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

• Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

• Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

• Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

• Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are

• Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

• Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python

• Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor

• Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

• Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line

• Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement

• Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

• High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

• Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

• Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

• Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well

• Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

• Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

- Seniorität & Verantwortung: Du bringst Deine Erfahrung aktiv ins Team ein, teilst Best Practices und unterstützt bei der Weiterentwicklung unserer Sales-Prozesse.

- Cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit internen Teams wie Marketing, Customer Success und Operations zusammen, um eine optimale Customer Experience sicherzustellen.

 

DEIN PROFIL

- Sales ist Deine Welt: Du verfügst über mindestens 1-3 Jahre Erfahrung im Vertrieb, idealerweise im B2B- oder SaaS-Umfeld.

- Proaktivität und Akquise-Talent: Du überzeugst durch exzellente Akquise-, Discovery- und Pitching-Skills.

- Erfahrung im Abschluss: Du hast nachweisbare Erfolge im eigenständigen Management eines Sales Funnels und im erfolgreichen Abschluss von Vertriebsprozessen.

- Entrepreneurial Mindset: Du bist ergebnisorientiert, verfügst über ein hohes Organisationsgeschick und behältst auch bei Herausforderungen den Fokus.

- Für unsere internen Trainings, All-Hands und den Austausch mit internationalen Kolleg:innen ist es hilfreich, wenn Du Englisch gut verstehen kannst. Falls Du Dich sprachlich noch weiterentwickeln möchtest, unterstützen wir Dich gerne mit entsprechenden Lernangeboten. Perfektes Englisch ist keine Voraussetzung. Deine Kundentermine finden auf Deutsch statt.

- Teamorientierung & Eigenverantwortung: Du arbeitest selbstständig, strukturiert und zuverlässig und hast Freude daran, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Dein Wissen mit anderen zu teilen.

Du bist der festen Überzeugung, dass Du genau das mitbringst, was es für die Position braucht? Dann ermutigen wir Dich, Dich zu bewerben. Selbst wenn Du nicht jede Anforderung erfüllst, bist Du vielleicht genau die/der richtige zukünftige Doctoliber:in für diese oder andere Stellen!

As a .NET Software Engineer, you'll be part of our agile team, working in the Scrum framework to deliver new features and improve existing ones in our subscription e-commerce platform, the multi-tenant B2B engine that powers global distributors. You'll own whole features within a product domain, from design to production, and work alongside experienced engineers who'll support your growth. You’re a curious and analytical engineer who sees the big picture but sweats the details. You enjoy diving into system architecture, making thoughtful trade-offs, and writing clean, testable code.

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset-AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

For more than a decade, Vasion has been helping companies simplify their print infrastructure, automate business processes, and integrate their technology in a more secure environment. Our mission, to make digital transformation attainable for everyone, drives a culture of innovation and exploration. We have one simple goal: help organizations simplify processes through automation and integration.

So we created simple, cost-effective, and easy-to-implement digital tools that work together, removing bottlenecks and improving efficiency. And we’re always on the lookout for new people who can help us innovate, grow, and reach our goal.

About the role

This role is remote, or hybrid for candidates within commuting distance of one of our offices in St. George or Lehi, UT.

Reporting to the Director, Digital Marketing, the Web Operations Manager is the operational engine of Vasion 's web team - the person who turns business requests into shipped pages and the person who keeps the team's delivery rhythm on track.

This role owns Vasion 's CMS day to day: building and editing pages and landing pages using existing components and templates, and knowing when a request can be handled directly versus when it needs to be scoped and handed to a developer or designer. This role also runs the team's operating cadence - standups, sprint planning, prioritization, and retros - and is the first stop for any stakeholder across Marketing who needs something from the web team. A big part of the job is translating a business ask ("we need a new campaign page," "this section needs to change") into a clear, actionable requirement someone can actually execute against, then following it through to done. Daily partners include web developers, UX/UI designers, the Head of Search & AI Visibility, content, customer marketing, growth marketing, and regional marketing managers.

What you'll do

CMS Management & Page Execution

• Build, edit, and publish webpages and landing pages directly in the CMS, using existing components and templates, based on business requests from across Marketing and the broader business

• Own the intake process for web requests: gather requirements, ask clarifying questions, and turn an ambiguous business ask into a clear, actionable spec

• Determine the right path for each request - execute it directly when it's within scope, or scope it and hand it to the right teammate (developer, UX/UI designer, etc.) when it requires new components or dev work

• Maintain governance over templates, components, and design-system usage across the site so pages stay consistent as more people request changes

• Handle redirect management, URL governance, and the ongoing consolidation of Vasion 's multi-brand web footprint

• Monitor Core Web Vitals, site speed, uptime, and overall page performance, and flag/triage issues as they come up

• Ensure pages meet accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 Level AA, WCAG 2.1 AA minimum), conducting basic accessibility checks and coordinating remediation with developers when issues are found

Team Operations & Delivery

• Run web team standups, sprint planning, prioritization meetings, and retros

• Build and maintain the roadmap for Vasion 's web and digital properties, and own sprint health (committed-work completion, blocker resolution, cycle time)

• Serve as the first point of contact for any stakeholder engaging the web team - triage inbound requests and turn them into scoped roadmap items

• Coordinate QA, cross-browser testing, regression testing, and releases with the development team

• Support localization and multi-region site execution in partnership with content and regional marketing teams

Search & Conversion Execution

• Implement technical SEO and AEO/GEO content structuring on pages, based on strategy and priorities set by leadership

• Build, QA, and ship CRO tests defined in partnership with leadership

• Surface technical feasibility and constraints back to leadership to help

We are looking for a skilled Application Security Engineer to support GuidePoint Security’s Application Security practice in the North Central region. This role will engage in the development of secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) programs, DevSecOps pipeline integrations, and security assessments of AI-enabled and agentic applications while providing “Wow Them” service to clients and/or internal customers or co-workers.
The Application Security Engineer will be required to demonstrate strong application security testing, DevSecOps automation, and secure code review skills, lead by influence, and strong business/financial acumen to drive the use of progressive application security, software supply chain, and AI security programs that will align the delivery business objectives and priorities.
About the North Central Application Security Practice
The North Central Application Security Practice is responsible for helping clients build, scale, and mature secure software development programs. We assess applications, embed security into engineering workflows, and advise development and security leaders across the organization.
Our team of application security engineers, consultants, and architects focuses on SAST, DAST, SCA, API and cloud-native security, software supply chain security, and the security of AI-enabled and agentic applications. We partner with client engineering, platform, and security teams to reduce risk without slowing delivery.

• DevSecOps and “shift-left” security automation across CI/CD pipelines

• Software supply chain security, including SBOMs, open-source risk, and artifact integrity

• Securing AI/LLM applications and agentic workflows against emerging threats

Roles and Responsibilities:

• Run and tune client SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets, and IaC scanning tools; triage results, eliminate false positives, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation guidance

• Design and implement security tool integrations into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Jenkins), source control, IDEs, and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow), including policy gates and break-the-build criteria

• Partner with development teams on remediation, secure coding guidance, and developer enablement to embed security throughout the SDLC

• Assess and harden software supply chain controls, including SBOM generation, dependency and container image scanning, artifact signing, and pipeline/runner security (e.g., SLSA)

• Perform threat modeling and security architecture reviews for cloud-native, microservice, container (Docker/Kubernetes), and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation) environments

• Leverage AI-assisted and agentic tooling (e.g., AI code assistants, automated triage, and auto-remediation workflows) to accelerate testing and reporting, and advise clients on the secure adoption of AI coding assistants

• Help clients mature AppSec programs by defining metrics, vulnerability management SLAs, and roadmaps aligned to frameworks such as OWASP SAMM, BSIMM, and NIST SSDF

• Produce clear, client-ready deliverables, present findings to technical and executive audiences, and contribute to the growth of the AppSec practice through tooling, methodologies, and knowledge sharing

title: Embedded Control Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

- Architect a breakthrough energy technology - Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion - Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

- Move fast and build what matters - Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

In this role, you will play a key part in developing the embedded control platform and will translate functional and control requirements into embedded hardware and software architectures, select appropriate microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA, or other controller technologies, and develop real-time software close to the hardware implementation. Your work will directly influence the performance, reliability, safety, and will require close collaboration with power electronics, integrated electronics, mechanical, thermal, and system engineers.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Define embedded controller architectures for power electronic converters and select suitable microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA.

- Translate power electronics and control requirements into efficient, deterministic, and robust real-time software implementations.

- Develop, test, debug, and validate embedded software on target hardware, from individual software blocks through complete controller implementations and automated testing environments to validate the design.

- Explore new controller technologies, embedded architectures, and software implementation concepts to improve converter performance, flexibility, reliability, functionality, and maintainability.

WHO YOU ARE

- You hold a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- You have a strong understanding of embedded architectures, and the practical considerations involved in selecting controllers for demanding real-time applications.

- You are an expert in embedded software development for real-time applications, preferably in power electronics, industrial automation, or similar applications, spanning FPGA programming, systems programming, hardware interfaces and communication protocols.

- You are experienced in monitoring and debugging software directly on target hardware

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with model-based development, hardware-in-the-loop testing, automated testing, or safety-critical software development is a plus.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

- Technical Screening (30 min)

- Technical Panel (3x60 min)

Through our specialized insurance expertise and field-based service model, we build lasting partnerships and deliver exceptional results for our customers. Our culture is built on collaboration, excellence, and a shared commitment to serving our customers and one another.

We take an extremely aggressive and proactive approach to claims adjusting and are looking for a person who not only knows their jurisdiction’s comp laws but also enjoys the role of putting that experience to good use. This is a remote position that requires working Pacific Time Zone business hours.

Responsibilities

• Manage California and Oregon workers' compensation claims from inception through resolution.

• Analyze claim facts and evaluate coverage, compensability, and benefits eligibility.

• Develop and execute strategies to achieve timely and favorable claim outcomes.

• Establish and maintain appropriate claim reserves.

• Negotiate settlements and bring about claim resolution.

• Communicate regularly with claimants, insureds, employers, and other stakeholders.

• Prepare and present large loss reports to internal and external audiences.

• Collaborate with defense counsel on litigation strategy and claim resolution.

• Partner with medical case managers, surveillance vendors, and other external resources.

• Ensure compliance with Illinois workers' compensation laws and regulations.

• Maintain accurate and timely claim documentation.

• Analyze claim trends and exposure to support effective decision-making.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Samsara's Telematics Business Unit - the company's oldest business line and the core of its revenue - is looking for a Principal Product Manager to take on a highly strategic, commercially-oriented mandate that cuts across the entire BU. In this role, you'll move fluidly between influencing company-wide strategic initiatives and hands-on building with engineering, reporting directly to the leader of the Telematics Business Unit.

This role exists to drive two things in parallel: step-function improvement in the core telematics business, and new, adjacent product bets that grow out of our core vehicle gateway (VG) products. • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Why this role is on the menu

The Senior Financial Insights Analyst sits at the center of Instacart's Finance organization, with a mandate to identify and close areas of P&L leakage through rigorous financial and transactional data analysis and compelling narratives that drive action. 

 

The team works through invoice challenges with retailers and serves as experts in the broader Instacart financial ecosystem. Invoicing retailers correctly is a key operational responsibility that impacts financial success and builds trust with retailer partners.

title: Marketing Manager
description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we're changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK's leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We're growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we're hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We're on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Content and events. Two engines of Flock's marketing, and you own the execution of both.

Today the marketing team is one Senior Marketing Manager, who owns the brand and website, publishes the content, launches the products and runs up to nine events a year, getting it all out of the door by pushing AI hard. We're doubling the team and backing it with 3.5x the budget.

You're the second person in, owning events and content.

Events. You'll plan the calendar with the Senior Marketing Manager and own delivery: trade shows and conferences, plus our own broker and customer events. On each one you'll set the budget, build the stand, run the day, chase the leads and report on whether it was worth repeating.

Content. You'll shape the strategy with the Senior Marketing Manager, then produce it. Volume and quality both count. LinkedIn and the Flock blog are the priorities, plus video and website copy. The stories sit with underwriting, distribution and product, so getting good material out of busy people is a big part of the job.

AI. Flock runs on AI and we build AI products for customers too. Marketing is held to the same standard. We want you to be the person who brings the newest tool into the office and shows everyone what it does. Brokers and customers still respond to work that feels human, so you'll be someone who writes excellently and still has creative flair.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

- Own social media. Run our social strategy, with LinkedIn as the primary channel: product videos, carousels, infographics, and PDF’s, posted consistently and measured for engagement.

- Create content at volume. Case studies, articles, industry news, thought leadership and product launch material, several times a month.

- Make video. Film and produce videos with our team in and around the office: people stories, product walkthroughs and interviews.

- Deliver events. Work with the Senior Marketing Manager Coordinate and execute our calendar of seven to nine events a year: trade shows, conferences and our own customer and broker events.

- Design your own assets in Claude Design and Figma, to a standard that holds up next to agency work.

- Work with AI daily. Draft, edit, repurpose and scale content with AI tools, applying your own voice and judgement so nothing reads machine-written.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Significant content creation and social media experience, ideally in B2B tech, with measurable results from owning and executing a social strategy.

- A portfolio of work you can share on the spot.

- Strong copywriting and communication, proven in published work.

- A track record organising and coordinating trade shows, conferences or business events, plus internal events for customers and stakeholders.

- Hands-on design skills in Figma and Claude Design. Adobe Creative Cloud would be a bonus.

- Startup pace and ownership: you've worked somewhere small enough to own outcomes end to end, spot what needs improving and act without waiting for a brief.

- Confident, critical use of AI across your marketing work.

Nice to have: video editing experience, and exposure to insurance, fleet or telematics.

title: Implementation Lead
description:
About TJM Labs

TJM Labs is building the digital workforce for pharmacy.
Pharmacies are being asked to do more with fewer resources. Prescription volumes are growing, margins are tightening, and talented pharmacy teams spend too much of their day on repetitive operational work.
We're changing that.
TJM Labs builds AI-powered automation designed specifically for pharmacy. Our technology works within the systems pharmacies already use to automate repetitive workflows and create more capacity for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians to focus on the work that actually requires them.
We're growing quickly, and successful implementation is one of the most important parts of delivering on that promise.
That's where you come in.
About the Role
We're looking for an Implementation Lead to own the day-to-day execution of customer implementations from discovery through go-live and transition to ongoing support.
This is a hands-on role at the intersection of pharmacy operations, project management, customer communication, and technology.
You'll work in close partnership with a Customer Success Manager (CSM). The CSM owns the overall customer relationship, strategic alignment, and escalations. You own getting the implementation done.
During implementation, you'll be the hub of the project. You'll coordinate customer and internal stakeholders, document how the pharmacy operates today, translate those workflows into clear requirements, maintain the implementation plan, manage communication and action items, own internal QA, and drive the project toward a successful go-live.
You'll also own one of the most important safeguards in our implementation process: making sure what the pharmacy does, what we've documented, what we've asked our technical teams to build, and what we ultimately deliver all remain in sync.
This isn't a role where you'll simply maintain a project plan and schedule meetings.
You'll ask questions. You'll uncover exceptions. You'll document details. You'll chase down decisions. You'll test what we've built. You'll notice when something doesn't line up. You'll keep people accountable for commitments. And when a project starts drifting, you'll help get it back on course.
You don't need to be an engineer or an AI expert.
You do need to understand pharmacy operations and pharmacy management systems, be curious about technology, communicate exceptionally well, and be very good at turning complexity into clarity.
What You'll Own
1. Day-to-Day Implementation Execution
Once a customer enters implementation, you'll own the day-to-day work required to get them live.

• Establish and maintain the implementation plan, milestones, dependencies, and target go-live date.

• Lead implementation meetings, discovery sessions, and working sessions.

• Coordinate activities across the pharmacy, TJM technical teams, the CSM, and other internal stakeholders.

• Track decisions, action items, customer deliverables, risks, dependencies, and outstanding requirements.

• Follow up consistently to keep projects moving.

• Identify risks and blockers early and drive them toward resolution.

• Manage implementation changes and understand their impact on scope, requirements, and timelines.

• Keep projects on schedule and surface concerns before they become surprises.

• Coordinate go-live activities and the transition into ongoing support.

At any point in the project, you should be able to answer: What needs to happen next to get this customer live?
2. Pharmacy Process Discovery & Documentation
Before we can automate a pharmacy workflow, we need to understand exactly how that workflow operates today.
You'll own creating and maintaining clear, accurate, and highly standardized documentation of each customer's current-state pharmacy processes before TJM automation is introduced.

• Lead structured workflow discovery with pharmacy stakeholders.

• Understand how work moves through the pharmacy today - including people, pharmacy management systems, other te

title: GNC Engineer (Guidance, Navigation & Control)
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Guidance, Navigation & Control Engineer at Applied, your role is pivotal. Your work will involve developing, integrating, and testing core flight autonomy capabilities that span all classes of aerial platforms (Group 1-5). You'll work closely with teams across the entire company to integrate core GNC algorithms into their software and product stacks, supporting applications in both commercial and defense spaces. The challenge is profound, and the rewards are immeasurable, as you build superior systems that empower our military with unrivaled capabilities.

AT APPLIED, YOU WILL:

- Write software that operates real autonomous aircraft systems including F16 fighter jets, group 1-5 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), as well as simulated models to accomplish tactical military missions

- Build, leverage, and improve aerial autonomy software architectures that are ultimately tested and deployed on real systems to accomplish military missions

- Collaborate with DoD warfighter domain experts and 3rd party UAS vehicle vendors to develop and integrate aerial autonomy software onto OEM hardware

WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

- Master's degree in Aerospace, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or similar field

- 6+ years of hands-on experience developing GNC software for autonomous systems

- Experience developing autonomy algorithms in either C++ or Python

- Experience developing or implementing outer-loop control systems or path planning algorithms

- Experience developing and simulating 3DoF or 6DoF models of air vehicles to support GNC algorithm development

- Experience with flight testing and performing data analysis

- Experience with UAS GNC/navigation systems such as PixHawk and Ardupilot

- Strong functional, procedural, data-oriented, and object-oriented programming experience

- Experience using git, Visual Studio Code, GitLab

Travel Requirements:

- Must be willing to travel as projects requires; estimated average travel is once every other month for between 2 days up to 1 week (~20%)

Security Requirements:

- Must be a U.S. Citizen

- Must hold or be eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance

NICE TO HAVE:

- Ability to use data visualization and debugging tools to support autonomy control development

- Experience developing in Docker and containerized development environments, using Linux-based operating systems (e.g., RHEL, Ubuntu), source control systems, and artifact registries

- Understanding of key technologies: C++, Python, DevOps, Containers, Linux

- Familiarity with software-in-the-loop (SIL)

title: Principal Mobile Engineer (POS Terminal)
description:
Who we are
Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.
About the role
As a Principal Mobile Engineer (POS-Terminal) at Moniepoint , you will be responsible for designing and leading the architecture of our POS terminal solutions across multiple platforms. You will ensure the scalability, security, performance, and reliability of our POS systems and related applications, including mobile apps for repair scheduling and maintenance. While the majority of our terminals are currently based on Android Native, your expertise in cross-platform solutions (e.g., Flutter, C, JavaScript) will be crucial as we expand and diversify our portfolio.You’ll play a critical role in shaping the direction of our POS-related products, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and ensuring the technical vision aligns with the company’s broader strategic goals.
Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.
What you will do:

• Lead the design and architecture of POS terminal solutions, ensuring security, scalability, performance, and integration with various hardware and payment systems.

• Develop and maintain architectural documents and diagrams for POS terminal systems, ensuring all platforms are well documented and up to date.

• Lead the development of POS-related applications

• Optimize system performance and security, particularly around payment processing and EMV protocols.

• Participate in planning sessions with product and engineering teams to ensure solutions meet market needs and business goals.

• Conduct code reviews and ensure best practices for mobile and embedded systems development, especially for Android Native development.

• Define and enforce software engineering best practices across the POS and related teams to improve efficiency and developer productivity.

• Ensure the stability and reliability of POS terminal products and applications, monitoring system performance and troubleshooting as necessary.

• Provide technical mentorship to engineering teams, helping them grow their skills and contribute to the broader technical vision.

• Participate in the hiring process, screening engineers with expertise in POS systems, mobile, and embedded development.

To succeed in this role, we think you should have:

• At least 8 years of experience in system design, architecture, and development, specifically in the POS terminal domain.

• Strong expertise in Android Native development (Java/Kotlin), with a deep understanding of Android-based POS terminal solutions.

• Experience in cross-platform mobile development, such as Flutter , and familiarity with other POS application platforms (e.g., C, JavaScript) is a plus.

• Strong knowledge of EMV (Europay, Mastercard, and Visa) security protocols, including chip-based transactions, encryption, and key management.

• Experience with hardware integration for POS devices, such as card readers, pin pads, printers, and other peripherals.

• Deep understanding of payment systems architecture , including integration with payment processors and gateways.

• Knowledge of software quality assurance principles and their application in financial systems.

• Excellent problem-solving skills with an ability to manage complex system interactions and adapt to changing requirements.
